'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Connie Mack III]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Bill Nelson]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsFL}} The '''2000 United States Senate election in Florida''' was held on November 7, 2000, the same date as the [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2000|U.S. House of Representatives]] and [[2000 United States presidential election|presidential election]]. Incumbent Republican Senator [[Connie Mack III]] decided to retire instead of seeking a third term. Democrat [[Bill Nelson]] won the open seat, even as Republican presidential nominee [[George W. Bush]] [[2000 United States presidential election in Florida|narrowly triumphed]] over [[Al Gore]] in the state by a mere 537 votes. [[Bill McCollum]]'s 46.19% popular vote percentage is the highest for a losing Republican United States Senate candidate in Florida. == Republican primary == === Candidates === * Hamilton A. S. Joel Deckard|Joel Deckard]], former U.S. representative from [[Evansville, Indiana]] (Reform) * [[Willie Logan]], state representative from [[Opa-locka, Florida|Opa-Locka]] (Independent) * [[Andy Martin]], perennial candidate (Independent) * [[Bill McCollum]], U.S. representative from [[Longwood, Florida|Longwood]] (Republican) * Darrell McCormick (Independent) * [[Bill Nelson]], [[Florida State Treasurer/Insurance Commissioner/Fire Marshal|Florida treasurer]], former U.S. representative (Democratic) * Joe Simonetta (Natural Law) === Campaign === This election was concurrent with the [[2000 United States presidential election in Florida|presidential election]], where Bush narrowly defeated Gore after an intense [[Florida recount|recount]]. The Senate election was evenly matched, with two U.S. congressmen named Bill in their mid-50s. Both parties heavily targeted this senate seat.{{Cite web|last=Dunkelburger|first=Lloyd|date=1 August 2000|title=Rep. McCollum raises stakes at Nelson fights|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=o0EgAAAAIBAJ&sjid=RH8EAAAAIBAJ&pg=6654,152782&dq=bill+mccollum+nelson&hl=en|url-status=live|access-date=2021-05-07|website=[[Sarasota Herald-Tribune]]|page=3A|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428025449/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=o0EgAAAAIBAJ&sjid=RH8EAAAAIBAJ&pg=6654,152782&dq=bill+mccollum+nelson&hl=en |archive-date=2016-04-28 }} The election became very nasty, as Nelson called his opponent "an extremist who would sacrifice the elderly, the poor, and the working class to coddle the rich." McCollum called the Democrat "a liberal who would tax everything that moves, and some things that don't." The election advertisements were very negative, as both candidates talked more about each other than themselves.{{cite web|last=Bragg|first=Rick|date=18 October 2000|title=The 2000 Campaign: A Florida Race; 2 Senate Candidates Eagerly Woo Moderates|url=https://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=FB0712FA3C5A0C7B8DDDA90994D8404482|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120714153120/http://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=FB0712FA3C5A0C7B8DDDA90994D8404482|archive-date=2012-07-14|access-date=2017-02-20|website=[[New York Times]]}} Nelson raised only [[soft money]],{{cite web|date=31 July 2000|title=Nelson Raises Million - and Heat|url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=MH&s_site=miami&p_multi=MH&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB72E5B1B1E71AA&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024111501/http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=MH&s_site=miami&p_multi=MH&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB72E5B1B1E71AA&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|archive-date=2012-10-24|website=[[Miami Herald]]|publisher=|page=1B}} but had help from Gore and President [[Bill Clinton]]. Two days before the election, McCollum predicted he would win by a 6-point margin.{{cite web|last=Zuckerman|first=Laura|date=2 November 2000|title=Rep. Mccollum Predicting 6-Point Victory Over Nelson|url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=NJ&p_theme=nj&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB51B511C29FC0A&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|url-status=live|access-date=2021-05-07|website=Nl.newsbank.com|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024111512/http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=NJ&p_theme=nj&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB51B511C29FC0A&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM |archive-date=2012-10-24 }} On election day, he lost by a five-point margin. ===Debates=== *[https://www.c-span.org/video/?159834-1/florida-senatorial-debate Complete video of debate], October 12, 2000 === Polling === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign="bottom" ! scope="col" |Poll source ! scope="col" |Date(s) ! scope="col" style="width:75px;" |Sample
